verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe self-hosting Trigger.dev on your own infrastructure with full control over environment, deployment and URLs. A Docker setup ships with a combined supervisor and a simple `docker compose up`, and the self-hosting overview gives version guidance (v4, with v3 support ending at 4.5.0). llms.txt describes it as an open source platform. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on reports of a self-hosted deployment working, documentation of feature parity with the cloud offering, and production-scale deployment guidance beyond Docker Compose.
